mechanism_narrative: Commuting recovery is the leading edge of retail recovery: TRANSIT rose monotonically across the four snapshot weeks (-32.1, -24.1, -11.1, -6.7) and each incremental transit trip restores weekday footfall in retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean of -27.0.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly means rose monotonically from -32.1 at t-3w to -6.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is at or below -27.0 even though TRANSIT continues to improve or holds above -10 for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossed into positive territory (+4.7, +4.1) after four weeks of recovery, which marks full restoration of routine errand behaviour; households that resume routine errands restart adjacent discretionary shopping within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC immediately.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -15.4 at t-3w to +4.7 at t-1w and +4.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above +3 for the next week while RETAIL_REC's mean over the following 7 days is below its prior 7-day mean of -20.2.

regime_hint: reopening with no new stay-home instructions
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stays below +0.5 for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 14 days is at or below its prior 14-day mean of -20.2.

candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -24.0 percent change
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -34.4 at t-3w to -23.4 at t-0w, crossing -24 at t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES holds above -24 for the next four weeks while RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days stays at or below -27.0.

mechanism_narrative: End-of-summer outdoor leisure is unwinding (PARKS fell from +0.3 to -4.6) while indoor errand activity is already positive (GROCERY_PHARM +4.1); this pairing signals a seasonal reallocation of discretionary time and spend from parks into indoor retail, which lifts RETAIL_REC over two weeks.

regime_hint: autumn transition with no containment measures
failure_condition: PARKS falls for two more weeks with GROCERY_PHARM still positive, yet RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 14 days is at or below its prior 14-day mean of -20.2.

mechanism_narrative: With no new containment measures in force, the joint improvement of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is a policy-driven release of suppressed demand; each week both series stay above the t-0w levels converts latent demand into visits, so RETAIL_REC's four-week mean continues to climb.
evidence_refs: fact:no new restriction appears in the snapshot and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: sustained reopening with no new containment measures
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both hold at or above their t-0w values (-6.7 and -23.4) for four weeks while RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is at or below -27.0.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT minus RETAIL_REC weekly gap widens beyond 12 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC was -20.0 at t-1w and -20.4 at t-0w while TRANSIT improved from -11.1 to -6.7, a 13.7 point gap at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening in which non-retail out-of-home purposes recover first

mechanism_narrative: A renewed containment impulse would first show up as a reversal in out-of-home series: if PARKS breaks below -10 and TRANSIT falls by more than 3 points week-on-week, retail visits are curtailed by the same measures, pushing RETAIL_REC's four-week mean below its trailing value.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below -10.0 and TRANSIT drops more than 3 points week-on-week
